prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you put ketchup on a hot dog in the city of Chicago. Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts microphone, glances nervously at the packed hearing room*

Mr. Chairman, members of the committee, I wish to state for the record that I am a loyal American. I have never been a member of the Communist Party, the Ketchup Party, or any organization dedicated to the overthrow of proper hot dog preparation.

* wipes brow *

However, I cannot invoke my Fifth Amendment rights here, because what we're discussing transcends the Constitution itself. Mr. Chairman, I was in Chicago on the date in question. I was young. I was foolish. The mustard line was long, and I—

* gasps from the gallery, a woman faints *

I WILL HAVE ORDER. The witness will continue.

* composes self *

Mr. Chairman, I put ketchup on that hot dog. Not because I was subversive. Not because I wished to offend the good people of this great city. But because I was—*voice breaks*—from out of town. I didn't know. The signs, the local customs, the very SPIRIT of the place... I was ignorant of them all.

* stares directly at camera *

But I have learned, Mr. Chairman. I have SEEN. I have watched the neon glow of Jimmy's Red Hots at midnight. I have stood in line at Portillo's in a driving rain. I understand now that a hot dog in Chicago is not food—it is a COVENANT. Sport peppers are not mere garnish; they are SACRAMENT.

* stands, arms raised *

So I ask this committee—not for mercy, but for UNDERSTANDING. Let me work in the mustard fields of the South Side. Let me atone through proper relish distribution. Let me prove that even a ketchup sinner may walk again in neon light!

* collapses into chair as gavel pounds *
